article.name: Daem0nMCP
article.summary: Daem0nMCP is a self-hostable MCP memory and decision-governance server. Its current v7 API routes opaque workspace-scoped calls through admission and covenant policy, stores semantic events with SQLite-backed canonical projections, and returns retrieval evidence with citation metadata. The README says v7 is not yet published.

who_what.text: The public project is hosted by the 9thLevelSoftware GitHub organization. The README describes Daem0nMCP as an AI-agent memory and decision-governance server with stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP transports.
The README states v7 is not yet published; this review describes current v7 source paths at the pinned head and treats older v6 passages as migration history.

architecture.text: The v7 code separates strict wire models, application routing/admission, workspace runtime resolution, operation handlers, the event store, and retrieval composition.

The server maintains workspace-local SQLite storage. Record operations describe memory_records as a canonical projection: semantic writes append through EventStore rather than mutating that projection directly. Projected record fields include type/content/hash, rationale/context/tags, relative file path, pin/archive state, outcome/worked state, scores, source client/model, source event ID, stream version, and timestamps.

Event commands carry workspace and stream identity, event type, occurred/recorded times, actor, payload, optional causation/correlation IDs, schema version and expected stream version. Append results include event/payload hashes, stream version and previous-event hash.

behavior.text: The memory_store_batch operation authorizes the workspace and passes records plus an idempotency key to the canonical batch writer. Projection scheduling follows successful writes.

Pin and archive changes are separate authorized operations and append memory.pin_set or memory.archive_set events; post-commit projection work is scheduled. This review did not trace all correction semantics.

The inspected record-operation mapping contains no per-record delete handler. The public v7 registry has separate destructive maintenance operations, including pruning and duplicate cleanup, but their full physical-erasure semantics were not traced; hard deletion remains unknown.

The public interface documents memory_recall, memory_search_text and file recall. The lexical path uses a bounded SQLite retrieval provider; the shared composer applies a token budget, emits citation-manifest entries and provider diagnostics, counts token usage, and can abstain when no policy-valid evidence remains.

V7 routing resolves an opaque workspace ID to a server-managed workspace and applies request admission/covenant policy before operation dispatch. The README documents workspace grants and linked-workspace behavior; explicitly federated retrieval can cross local workspace boundaries. Isolation quality was not tested.

Event records retain actor/time/stream/correlation and hash metadata; projected records retain source client/model and source event IDs. Retrieval evidence includes references, channels and applicability, while a citation manifest maps rendered citations to those references. This is lineage support, not a measured guarantee that generated claims are supported.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention — unmeasured. Retrieval and a no-policy-valid-evidence abstention path are implemented; no answer or abstention cases were adjudicated.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. Event appends and state-change events are source-visible; no correction workload was run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. A per-record deletion path and the full physical-erasure behavior of maintenance operations were not established.
Scope-isolation leakage — unmeasured. Workspace resolution and grants are documented; no paired allowed/forbidden workspace workload was run.
Evidence support precision and citation coverage — unmeasured. Evidence references and citation manifests are present; no generated claims were scored.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. No runtime timings were collected.
Tokens and cost — unmeasured. Retrieval tracks rendered token-budget usage, but no provider usage or charges were collected.
Storage efficiency — unmeasured. No workload-attributed logical or physical storage bytes were collected.

Source-visible controls include batched writes, idempotency, bounded workers/candidate counts, a SQLite search timeout, post-commit projection scheduling, token accounting and provider diagnostics. These are code observations, not benchmark results.

limits: The review covers selected v7 API, event, database, retrieval and operations-guide sources at one pinned head; it does not trace every provider, projection worker, migration, federation policy, client integration or maintenance path.
The README says v7 is not yet published; packaged release behavior may differ from the reviewed source.
The event append/projection design is visible, but complete correction semantics, transaction recovery, and physical deletion across maintenance paths are not established.
Workspace authorization and evidence models are source observations. Security outcomes, retrieval quality and answer grounding were not measured.
No Daem0nMCP runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed.
